**TL;DR**

- **Yesterday's rotation reversed.** S&P 500 **+0.58%** to 7,757.17, Nasdaq Composite **+1.05%** to 26,702.86, Dow +0.69% to 52,856.09, Russell 2000 +0.27%.
- **Technology led** (XLK +1.67%) for the first time this week; **communication services was the worst sector** (XLC -1.11%). Health care, yesterday's leader, gave it back (XLV -0.49%).
- **The Nasdaq's outperformance was narrow.** Equal-weight S&P (RSP) **+0.36%** vs SPY **+0.53%**; small caps (IWM +0.25%) *underperformed* the cap-weighted index. That is the mirror image of yesterday (RSP/SPY 3.4x).
- Today's rally was mega-cap-led, not broad.
- **Vol compressed again** — VIX 16.68 (-3.64%), VXN 24.42 (-3.17%). VIX is at its lowest since 10-13. 10-year yield 5.146% (+3bp).
- **The 20-year auction stopped at 5.469%** — the **highest since January 1986** — with a 0.9bp tail and soft indirect demand (58.2%, -7.0pts vs average).
- Long end is inverted: 20Y 5.469% > 30Y 5.413% > 10Y 5.106%.
- **After-hours:** **META +6.08%** to $739.90 on a Q3 beat (revenue $64.60B, +26%; ex-charge EPS $7.40). **TSLA +1.35%** to $391.68 (Q3 FCF +$1.53B vs -$4.51B expected; Musk confirms Tesla/SpaceX merger committees).
- **LRCX -6.07%** to $244.97 — a beat-and-raise that sold off hard.
- **Two big single-name reversals in the session:** **AT&T -6.45%** (beat + raised EPS guide, but net debt/EBITDA jumped to 3.13x) and **Arcus -19.58%** (casdatifan data sell-the-news + lung-cancer trial halt).
- **Tomorrow (Oct 22):** WDC, VLO, NEM, CMCSA, BE report; **$26B 5-yr TIPS auction at 1:00 PM ET**; jobless claims 8:30 AM.

**5. After-hours earnings reactions**

**Meta (META) — Q3 2026, released after the close, call 16:30 ET → **+6.08% to $739.90****

([press release via marketscreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/meta-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-ce785cd9dd8cf620))

- **Metric**: Revenue · **Q3 2026**: $64,601M · **Q3 2025**: $51,242M · **Change**: +26% (reported and cc)
- **Metric**: Costs and expenses · **Q3 2026**: $51,613M · **Q3 2025**: $30,707M · **Change**: +68% (incl. $9.89B legal charge)
- **Metric**: Income from operations · **Q3 2026**: $12,988M · **Q3 2025**: $20,535M · **Change**: -37% (margin 20% vs 40%)
- **Metric**: Ex-charge income from operations · **Q3 2026**: $22,988M · **Q3 2025**: — · **Change**: —
- **Metric**: Net income · **Q3 2026**: $9,860M · **Q3 2025**: $2,709M · **Change**: +264%
- **Metric**: Diluted EPS (GAAP) · **Q3 2026**: $3.83 · **Q3 2025**: $1.05 · **Change**: +265%
- **Metric**: Diluted EPS ex-charge · **Q3 2026**: $7.40 · **Q3 2025**: — · **Change**: vs consensus $6.54–$6.85

- **Revenue beat the top of the company's own $61–64B guide** and consensus (~$63.2–63.3B). Ad revenue $63,061M (+26%). **DAP 3.64B (+3%)**, ad impressions **+10%**, average price per ad **+14%**.
- The headline GAAP figures are wrecked by a **$9.89B charge** for the August agreement with **52 state attorneys general** on teen mental health/social-media litigation (payments of up to ~$18.59B over ten years).
- Ex-charge EPS of $7.40 is the comparable number. Effective tax rate 24% vs 87% LY.
- **Q4 2026 revenue guide $73–76B** (Street ~$73.6B); FX an ~1% headwind. **FY26 total expenses raised to $175–179B** (from $165–169B) for the charge. **Reality Labs 2026 losses now $18–19B.**
- **No 2027 revenue outlook and no 2027 capex number** — the single biggest watch item. The Street pencils ~$186B for 2027 capex vs $130–145B guided for 2026.
- Also announced the **establishment of a new Class C common stock**.
- Context: META fell **-8.6% and -8.0%** after its last two reports; options had priced a **±6–7%** move.
- A +6% reaction is a relief move, and it came despite the missing 2027 capex figure.
- After-hours bar: 697.52 → 739.90.

**Tesla (TSLA) — Q3 2026, released after the close, call 17:30 ET → **+1.35% to $391.68****

([Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/10/21/tesla-tsla-q3-2026-financial-results/), [eletric-vehicles](https://eletric-vehicles.com/tesla/tesla-q3-adjusted-profit-beats-estimates-as-cash-flow-defies-forecast-burn/))

- **Metric**: Revenue · **Q3 2026**: $28.05B · **Q2 2026**: $28.24B · **Q3 2025**: $28.10B (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: Total gross margin · **Q3 2026**: 19.6% · **Q2 2026**: 16.8% · **Q3 2025**: 18.0% (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: Auto gross margin ex-credits · **Q3 2026**: 18.1% · **Q2 2026**: 16.3% · **Q3 2025**: 15.4% (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: Operating income · **Q3 2026**: $718M · **Q2 2026**: $398M · **Q3 2025**: $1,624M (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: Operating margin · **Q3 2026**: 2.6% · **Q2 2026**: 1.4% · **Q3 2025**: 5.8% (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: GAAP net income / EPS · **Q3 2026**: $787M / $0.22 · **Q2 2026**: $1.11B · **Q3 2025**: $1.37B (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: Non-GAAP EPS · **Q3 2026**: $0.48 · **Q2 2026**: $0.33 · **Q3 2025**: $0.50 (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: Free cash flow · **Q3 2026**: +$1.53B · **Q2 2026**: -$1.09B · **Q3 2025**: +$3.99B (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: Capex · **Q3 2026**: $4.73B · **Q2 2026**: $5.79B · **Q3 2025**: $2.25B (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)
- **Metric**: Energy storage deployed · **Q3 2026**: 13.7 GWh · **Q2 2026**: 13.5 GWh · **Q3 2025**: 12.5 GWh (+1 more column(s) in the artifact table)

- **The cash line is the story.** FCF came in $6.0B better than the Street expected because capex ran $3.0B *below* guidance.
- Operating cash flow $6.26B; cash and investments $45.4B (+$1.9B); TTM revenue above $100B for a second straight quarter.
- **Energy**: revenue $4.61B (+33%), segment gross margin **33%** (from 20% in Q2), gross profit $954M (from $1.07B LY). Storage deployment **missed** at 13.7 GWh vs ~15.9 GWh.
- **Auto**: revenue $20.56B (-3%); ASP ex-FX ~$41,900 (roughly flat); cost per vehicle ~$34,500 (from $35,700). Regulatory credits **$113M**, -73% y/y — that line is not coming back.
- Deliveries 486,532 (-2.1% y/y, +1.3% q/q) vs consensus ~462,000; production 464,391; "other models" (Cybertruck, Semi, Model S/X) **-48% to 8,295**.
- Sold 22,141 more than it built; inventory down to 11 days of supply from 15.
- **"Battery availability continued to be the limiting factor"**, and the company cites its **largest passenger-vehicle backlog in four years**.
- **Musk confirmed Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to weigh a merger** ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/20/spacex-spcx-earnings-live-updates-q3-2026html.html)).
- FSD (Supervised) attach rate >75% of new North American deliveries (~+20pts q/q); ~2M cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles.
- **Data-integrity note:** one secondary outlet (Teslarati) published a results summary whose figures — $28.095B revenue, $0.50 adj EPS, 5.8% operating margin, $1.624B operating income, +$3.99B FCF —
- are **identical to Q3 2025 actuals**, not today's print. The numbers above are from two independent outlets that agree with each other and with the consensus framework.

**Lam Research (LRCX) — Sept 2026 quarter, released 16:05 ET, call 17:00 ET → **-6.07% to $244.97****

([press release via Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20695323-lam-research-corporation-reports-financial-results-for-the-quarter-ended-september-27-2026))

- Revenue **$8,219M** vs guide $8.10B ±$400M and consensus ~$8.14B — **beat**. Non-GAAP EPS **$2.20** vs guide $2.15 ±$0.15 and consensus ~$2.18 — **beat**.
- Non-GAAP gross margin 52.4%, operating margin **40.2%** (from 37.4% in June). Revenue +22% q/q, +54% y/y. Cash $7.45B (from $5.60B).
- December-quarter guide: revenue **$8.60B ±$400M**, gross margin 52.5% ±1%, operating margin 40.5% ±1%, EPS $2.33 ±$0.15.
- **The stock fell 6% anyway.** *Assessment (my read, not a sourced attribution):* the December guide implies **+4.6% q/q against +22% delivered**, and the equity has been de-rating all month —
- a record ten-session losing streak into the print, a trailing P/E near 59x versus a five-year median near 24x, and Evercore ISI trimming to $315 from $355 on "late-cycle multiple-compression concerns." The 17:00 call's 2027 WFE commentary is the unresolved variable.
- **Action: read the 17:00 call transcript before trusting this print.** The AH move is a 39-minute-old reaction to a headline, not a verdict.

**AT&T (T) — Q3 2026, reported before the open → **-6.45% to $21.91****

([FT company announcement](https://markets.ft.com/data/announce/detail?dockey=600-202610210630CANADANWCANADAPR_C2239-1), [investing.com](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/att-q3-2026-slides-strong-growth-overshadowed-by-debt-concerns-93CH-4923007))

- **Beat and raised**: revenue $32.3B (+5.3%); adjusted EPS **$0.65** vs $0.60 consensus (beat by 8.3%); adjusted EBITDA $12.5B (+5.4%); FCF $5.0B; record **769,000** internet net adds (442,000 fiber);
- >1M Advanced Connectivity adds for a second straight quarter. **2026 adjusted EPS guide raised to "the $2.40 range"** from $2.25–$2.35, with long-term capex lowered to $23–24B (2026) and $22–23B (2027–28).
- **The market sold the balance sheet**: net debt **$149.8B from $126.4B** after the EchoStar spectrum purchase (+$23B of debt), taking **net debt/adjusted EBITDA to 3.13x from 2.68x**.
- Roughly $8B of market cap erased.
- Also soft: postpaid phone adds 379,000 (down from 432,000 in Q2) and **postpaid phone churn up to 0.92% from 0.86%** —
- with SpaceX's Starlink Mobile spectrum push an overhang (knocked ~6.6% off the shares on 10-09).
- GAAP EPS from continuing operations fell to $0.13 (a $2.6B Mexico impairment plus separation charges; the year-ago quarter carried a $0.79 DIRECTV gain).
- **VZ reports 10-26 and TMUS 10-28** — that is the tell on whether this is AT&T-specific or a sector repricing.
- Volume 83.7M = 182% of the 3-month average. After hours: flat (+0.18%).

**Arcus Biosciences (RCUS) — **-19.58% to $19.10**, -2.46% after hours**

- **Sell-the-news on the ARC-20 casdatifan data** presented at the 10-20 investor event: 1L PFS 86% at 6 months / 69% at 12 months (50% confirmed response rate);
- 2L + cabozantinib median PFS 14.5 months vs a ~10-month external benchmark; pooled late-line 35-month median OS, 13-month median PFS, 36% CR.
- Investor Day framed a **$5–10B RCC opportunity**; Phase 3 PEAK-20 to start by year-end.
- **Truist said 2L PFS fell short of its expectations and 1L durability is unproven.** Wedbush raised its target to $49 (from $43), Truist to $41 (from $40), HC Wainwright also raised.
- Separately, **Arcus halted the Phase 3 STAR-121 lung-cancer trial after a futility review, and Gilead declined to extend its option.** Q3 earnings 10-27.
